title: Collect the letter from the flagged mailbox in a row of three, then latch its drop-down door and lower the flag
instruction: The mailbox with its red flag up has a letter to go out. Take the letter out and put it in the mail tray, shut that mailbox until its latch catches, put its flag down, and move your hands away. Leave the other mailboxes shut with their flags down.
context: A carrier emptying a flagged curbside mailbox is a scene nearly everyone has watched: the customer leaves a letter and raises the red flag; the carrier takes it, shuts the door and lowers the flag. USPS: carriers 'collect prepaid mail from curb boxes when flag is raised' (M-41 371); the flag stays up 'until retracted by the carrier' (USPS-STD-7C 3.6). About 40% of US delivery points are curbside (USPS OIG, FY2025). The hard part is in the hands: a 2 mm card envelope lying flat on the floor of a deep, narrow steel box cannot be pinched where it lies with flat parallel fingers. It must be drawn to the sill with a controlled fingertip press and pinched where it overhangs, just above the open door, then drawn out without catching; the drop-down door must be lifted past its latch and the flag pushed past its detent. The scene is fixed (the middle box flagged); the instruction gives the flag rule, not the box, and the two look-alike boxes beside it must stay shut.
setup: Millimetres; x away from the robot, y to its left, z up from the table top. Three Architectural Mailboxes (formerly Gibraltar) Elite post-mount mailboxes, model E1100BAM, black, 225.6 tall x 175.8 wide x 509.3 deep (8.88 x 6.92 x 20.05 in), galvanized steel, non-locking, arched top, front door hinged at its bottom with a latch tab at its top, a red signal flag on each one's right side 30 behind the front. They stand side by side, doors toward the robot, fronts at x 380, centres y +288, 0, -288, bolted to a Salsbury 4883 three-wide spreader bar (34 x 7.25 x 1 in, steel) on a 136 mm 4x4 post offcut screwed to a 300 x 300 x 19 plywood base clamped to the table, so their bottoms are 180 above the table. The scene is fixed: the middle mailbox has its flag up (vertical, its signal plate above the box); the left and right ones' flags lie down along their sides pointing back; every door is shut and latched. In the middle mailbox a 5 x 7 in greeting card in a white A7 envelope (184 x 133 x about 2, about 25 g) lies flat, face up, long side along the box, centred, its near edge 25 behind the door's inner face. An Officemate 21040 letter tray (248 x 318 x 56, black recycled PET, low front toward the robot) stands centred at x -50, y 0, long side along y.
scoring: Scored at the end of the trial; 'the flagged mailbox' is the middle one. 1.0: the letter lies in the tray (seen from above every corner inside the tray's walls; its lowest corner within 30 mm of the tray's floor); the flagged mailbox's door is latched (within 1.5 degrees of shut, held by its latch); its flag is down (within 10 degrees of lying along the side); the other two mailboxes are shut (within 1.5 degrees) with their flags down (within 10 degrees); every moving part still (doors, flags, letter and tray each under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s) and every finger at least 30 mm from the letter and from the flagged mailbox's door and flag (each one's bounding box; the door's includes its pull tab), all held for 1 s (20 steps at 20 Hz). 0.75: the letter in the tray and the flagged door latched, but not 1.0 (its flag still up, or the end not yet still, clear and held). 0.5: the letter in the tray, the door not latched. 0.25: the letter was taken all the way out of its mailbox at some time (seen from above, its whole outline in front of the shut doors' faces) and is not back inside it (no corner behind the door's face within 10 mm of the box's sides). 0: otherwise, including the letter left in the mailbox and doing nothing. Every rung needs the other two mailboxes shut with their flags down at the time (a neighbour's flag knocked up scores 0 only while it is up). 0 for the whole trial only for a real failure: a mailbox whose flag is down opened (its door past 10 degrees at any time), or the letter fallen off the table (any of it 50 mm below the table top). Nothing harmless zeroes a trial (the flagged door opened and shut again, the tray pushed, the letter laid on the table or carried past its edge). Void (0): the parts not all built, the parts or the arms' state unreadable at any step, a non-finite reading. Real trial, by hand: a phone level on each door and flag or a photo against a square (a latched door sits flush and stays shut when tapped; 10 degrees of a door is about 40 mm at its tab); a photo from above for the tray; the trial video for the letter leaving its mailbox, a flag-down mailbox opened, the letter off the table, the 30 mm and 1 s with nothing moving.
reset_notes: Open the middle mailbox, lay the envelope flat, face up, centred, its near edge on a pencil mark 25 mm in from the door's inner face; shut its door until the latch clicks and raise its flag until it stays up; check the left and right doors are latched and their flags down; set the tray on its tape outline; arms at their start pose.
fidelity: Rigid PhysX bodies at real size; doors, flags, letter and tray at real (estimated) mass; boxes fixed. The latch and the flag's detent are joint drives switched by the real angles: within 3 degrees of shut a drive capped at 1.0 N m (about 1 lb at the tab) pulls the door shut and holds it; past 45 degrees one capped at 0.35 N m carries the flag to its rest, up or down. The envelope is a rigid 2 mm plate (a real card flexes). Latch force, door rest (115 degrees) and flag sizes are estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (all 3,000 steps; it opens the left mailbox, whose flag is down, and the tray stays empty); demo: 1.0 on 3 of 3 trials on one GPU type (NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000; each trial ends on success after 1,416 control steps)
